name: Merging equal fault gadgets
summary: Two fault gadgets for the same fault, of weights w₁ and w₂, merge into one of weight min(w₁, w₂).
description:
Faults are described here by their $Z$-flips: a green spider (connected by a fault-free edge to the rest of the diagram) with a one-legged green spider attached by a noisy edge describes a $Z$-flip of the given weight. Two such gadgets on the same spider, of weights $w_1$ and $w_2$, describe the same fault twice; they are fault-equivalent to a single gadget of weight $\min(w_1, w_2)$, since only the cheapest way to produce a fault matters, and producing it twice has no effect.

As in the paper, noisy edges are labelled with their weight (the cost of a flip on that edge; a vector of weights for the $X$-, $Y$- and $Z$-flips, unlabelled noisy edges have weight 1), and *fault-free* (idealised) edges are drawn bold purple. These annotations are shown on the rule as stated; derived variants (transpose, colour swap, other legs counts) may drop them.
